definition: Physical artificial intelligence or physical AI refers to artificial intelligence (AI) systems that perceive, reason about and act within the physical world.
details: These systems generally combine AI models with sensors, control systems, actuators and physical machines such as robots or autonomous vehicles. Physical AI overlaps with embodied artificial intelligence, robotics and autonomous systems, but it emphasizes the complete process of perceiving an environment, motion planning an action and physically executing the task to perform work. This differs from digital AI or generative AI (GenAI), which primarily stays in the information or digital realm. The term became increasingly prominent during the AI boom in the 2020s as AI development expanded from primarily digital applications toward humanoid robots, self-driving vehicles, smart factories and other autonomous machines. Its boundaries are not standardized, and it is often treated as a continuation of earlier research in robotics and embodied intelligence rather than an entirely separate field.

explainer.lead: Physical AI refers to AI systems that perceive, reason about and act within the physical world. It matters because it joins AI models to sensors, actuators and machines to perform actual work, unlike digital or generative AI that stays in the information realm.

tiers.eli5: It is AI with a body: it sees its surroundings, plans a move and then actually does something, like a robot picking up an object.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers combine AI models with sensors, control systems, actuators and physical machines such as robots or autonomous vehicles; a pitfall is treating it like digital AI when the full perceive-plan-execute loop must work in the real world.
tiers.paperLevel: Physical AI systems perceive an environment, perform motion planning for an action and physically execute the task to perform work; it overlaps with embodied AI, robotics and autonomous systems.

explainer.example: A warehouse robot perceives its surroundings, plans a path and physically moves to pick up a package.
